scope: count-based memory attribution and mixed-mode lifecycle diagnosis on macOS; not formal performance acceptance

protocol.original_timing_report_usage: pixel hashes only; no prior timing score or epsilon reused

conclusion: Single-case device peaks and logical working sets decrease. Mixed-mode retention nonregression is not established: two stable post-cleanup footprint comparisons exceed measured epsilon, while natural-idle R/R calibration is unstable. No speed or PR acceptance.
limitations: No E FPS/latency score was collected.
AOT intermediate attribution is not a named-edge spatial-local decomposition, so the formal local-memory benefit gate remains unassessed.
GPU-safe allocation intervals are conservative CPU-observation bounds.
Only light workers supply device-total and process-footprint results.
Worst observed differences compare maximum E with minimum R; both B0/B1 references are retained.
Natural-idle and explicit context-destroy/pool-release observations are separate phases.
Reference process-lifetime peaks are unstable for Portra 4K in both original arms; they are not accepted despite lower observed C values.
Post-cleanup process-footprint excess has not been attributed; a leak or a specific cache is not established.
GPU dispatch counts increase greatly; no E latency/FPS measurements were made, so observed speedup or slowdown is not established.
R-B1 is a named original comparison arm, not a frozen four-case B_ref.
The existing clean-R Swift exact no-op failure remains recorded in stage three; this stage does not make the full test suite green.
